what: It supplies workers to airport cargo, ground handling and passenger service companies in Hong Kong.
proceeds: It plans to use the money to improve operations with technology, hire more skilled staff and grow, build its brand in aviation, and fund working capital and general needs. It expects about US$27,510,000 in net proceeds at a US$5.00 share price.
risks: The Cayman holding company relies on its Hong Kong subsidiary for cash, and any limit on payments to it could hurt the business.
China could limit moving money out of Hong Kong, or change rules in ways that raise costs or make the shares worthless.
The company may become subject to Chinese rules on overseas listings and data security, and failing to comply could seriously harm it.
